q-us45-dok2-8.explanation: Before 1935 an employer could fire a worker simply for joining a union. The Wagner Act made union membership, collective bargaining and striking legally protected and created the NLRB to enforce them. The change was legal standing, not wages: workers could now negotiate as a body rather than one at a time.
